clue.text: Directed song with a gentle piano introduction

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the front, so these letters lead in before the song

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical marking for soft or gentle playing
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A conductor or arranger guided a song that opens with soft piano playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gentle' and 'piano' both give P, the musical marking for soft playing; 'introduction' puts A, P, P before LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort that is applied or directed is aimed at a particular target, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: One losing heart when taken in by a business graduate, low form of life

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word one goes

parts.note: the word one taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses courage after being taken on by an MBA, and is thought a low form of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' cuts the middle N from ONE, leaving OE, which 'taken in by' puts inside A + MBA.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism is the textbook example of a primitive, simple creature.

clue.text: Old man to settle on a tree

parts.note: an old man is a father, informally pa
to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Father is told to come to rest on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical fruit grows on a small tree of the same name, the pawpaw.

clue.text: Starts small educational organisation with one rich philanthropist

parts.note: Inst is the short form of institute, a college or educational body
I is the Roman numeral one
Bill Gates, the very rich Microsoft founder known for his charitable foundation

explanation.surface: A tiny college gets going with backing from a wealthy donor.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something going or provoke it, so it means starts in the verb sense.

clue.text: Discharge journalist that's upset common people

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist
the mob is the common people or rabble

explanation.surface: An editor gets the sack for upsetting ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's upset' turns ED round to give DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is the informal British term for discharging someone from the armed forces after a war.

clue.text: Old king advances, one first person replacing another

indicators.note: replacing another means one pronoun takes the place of a second pronoun in the word

parts.note: to advance money or a proposal is to raise it
I is the other first-person pronoun
me is a first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch makes progress, one person swapping in for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: In RAISES the pronoun I is swapped for the pronoun ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses was the name of several pharaohs of ancient Egypt, Rameses II being the best known.

clue.text: Deter swimming around island for one particular swimmer

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters are placed on either side of the island
letters that are swimming are moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A swimmer circles an island as a deterrent, one sort of fish in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns DETER into RED + ET, which goes 'around' MULL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reddish food fish of the Mediterranean, a specific kind of sea creature that swims.

clue.text: Stubborn person making a mess, wasting day after day

indicators.note: wasting means using up and losing, so letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a muddle is a mess
D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give two Ds

explanation.surface: An obstinate type makes a mess, frittering away one day after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' removes both Ds from MUDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is proverbially obstinate, so the animal's name is used for a pig-headed individual.

clue.text: Two instructions to be violent to achieve great success

definitions.text: Two instructions to be violent to achieve great success

parts.words: Two instructions to be violent to achieve great success
parts.note: two violent commands, to break something and to strike, together make a phrase for a huge popular triumph

explanation.surface: Violence is recommended twice as the route to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words of the answer are commands to use force: one to break something, one to strike it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is everyday slang for a hugely popular record, show or film.

clue.text: Cleaning waste water up in to-and-fro action

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a swing moves to and fro

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters climb, so they read backwards

parts.note: pee is urine, waste water from the body

explanation.surface: Dirty water is splashed about in a back-and-forth motion while tidying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEE into EEP, which goes 'in' SWING after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping with a broom is a basic household cleaning task, so the gerunds match.

clue.text: Colleagues work, given retrospective concession

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: Coworkers' efforts earn a belated sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns SOP round into POS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppos, short for opposite numbers, is informal British slang for mates or colleagues.

clue.text: Time of life that's featured in tragedy

definitions.text: Time of life that's featured in tragedy

parts.words: Time of life that's featured in tragedy
parts.note: a stage of life, and also the three letters a-g-e that sit at the very centre of the word tragedy

explanation.surface: A period of life is depicted in a tragic play.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the word for a period of life sits in the centre of 'tragedy', between TR and DY.
explanation.definitionFit: The years roughly between forty-five and sixty-five are the stage of life known by this phrase.

clue.text: Officers getting negligent little sleeper to admit wickedness

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Little Boy Blue in the nursery rhyme fell asleep under the haystack instead of minding the sheep
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Police officers persuade a careless child who nodded off to confess his misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Boy Blue is a nursery-rhyme shepherd boy found asleep. 'to admit' places SIN between BOY and BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British informal name for police officers, from their blue uniforms.

clue.text: See 20
End of fine game in topping sport

indicators.note: in means set inside the other word

parts.note: icing is a topping on a cake

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: skat is a German three-handed card game

explanation.surface: A good game finishes in some top-quality sport.
explanation.walkthrough: E (the last letter of 'fine') plus SKAT goes 'in' ICING after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding on blades over a frozen surface is a recreation and Winter Olympic event.

clue.text: Alan is chap involved in energised rapping — American music

indicators.note: in means set inside the other set of letters
energised suggests lively movement, so these letters are scrambled too
involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man named Alan gets caught up in some lively rap — very American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energised' turns RAPPING into AP + PRING, and 'involved' turns ALAN IS CHAP into PALACHIANS, which goes 'in' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland's ballet score of 1944 is a landmark piece of American orchestral music.

clue.text: One paid US seller for food

parts.note: a pro, or professional, is one paid for their work
vender is the American spelling of vendor, a seller

explanation.surface: A paid American salesman is looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is an old-fashioned or humorous word for provisions, especially animal fodder.

clue.text: Attempts to keep university workshops

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the university goes within

parts.note: a shy is an attempt, as in having a shy at something
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to stop a university from slipping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts MIT inside SHIES after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's forge, a kind of workshop, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Californian good guy? Individual on the up

parts.note: an angel is a thoroughly good person

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A Californian is a decent fellow, someone whose fortunes are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns ONE round into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native or resident of Los Angeles, a city in California.

clue.text: Clue to a host offering euphemistic expressions?

parts.note: the letters of the word oaths, chopped up and rearranged as if minced, spell these two clue words

explanation.surface: A hint is given to someone hosting a party about polite substitutes for swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'minced' is an anagram signal, and shuffling OATHS gives A HOST, the words of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced oaths are mild substitutes for swearwords, such as gosh or heck, so they are euphemisms.

clue.text: See 14
Demand of union prevented trader doing business

definitions.meaning: a trade union's requirement that every worker in a workplace belongs to it
a retailer that is not open, and so cannot trade

explanation.surface: A union's demand stopped a shopkeeper from trading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an arrangement where only union members may be employed, and literally describes a shop not open for trade.

clue.text: Report of contemptible person being kicked

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome, contemptible person

explanation.surface: A rumour spreads that some nasty individual got a kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Toed means struck with the toe, so it serves as a past participle for kicked.

clue.text: Dealt with chum needing to collect a vehicle — something in hand

parts.note: to meet a demand is to deal with it, so met means dealt with
a car is a vehicle
a pal is a chum

explanation.surface: A friend who has to pick up a car is sorted out, with something to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A metacarpal is one of the five bones of the palm, so it is literally inside the hand.

clue.text: Bad son kicked out of seat

indicators.note: kicked out of means expelled, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a saddle is a seat on a horse or bicycle

explanation.surface: A naughty boy is thrown off his seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked out of' drops the S from SADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Addle as an adjective, now rare, means rotten, as an addled egg has gone off.

clue.text: My friend ultimately finishes on good terms with English composer

indicators.note: finishes means comes at the end, placing that letter last

parts.note: to be well in with someone is to be on good terms with them
Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A friend of mine finally completes his work while on friendly terms with an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes' puts D, the last letter of 'friend', after WELL IN + E + VERDI. 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the interjection My! can be swapped for the longer phrase.

clue.text: See 24 Down
More than one climber is having inner struggle

indicators.note: having something inner means holding it inside, so the word is placed within

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Someone climbing has an internal battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having inner' puts VIE inside IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a climbing plant, so the plural means several climbers.

clue.text: Returning engineer flaps about nothing — one who says too much

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters go round the nothing
returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
lips are flaps of flesh round the mouth
O is the round shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An engineer comes back, flapping about over nothing, and blabs too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns RE + LIPS into SPILER, which goes 'about' O after its SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler gives away a plot twist or ending, revealing more than people wanted to hear.

clue.text: Busy with aim to embrace something green?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
a gage, as in greengage, is a green plum

explanation.surface: Busy with a goal of hugging something green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts GAGE inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or toilet that is engaged is in use, or busy in American usage.
